findings.title: Upsampled count sums sample_weight but nothing stores that weight
findings.body: upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) and is substituted for count() on allowlisted error queries. This change never writes sample_weight and never computes an inverse sample rate. The only data-path edit, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling in the test factory, copies contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate (for example 0.1) onto the existing event field sample_rate, which is the server-side sampling rate, not a weight. ClickHouse sum skips nulls, and the aggregate does not use ifNull(sample_weight, 1), so events with a missing weight contribute nothing; toInt64 then truncates a fractional sum toward zero, so a stored rate of 0.1 becomes 0 rather than 10. OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint only catches ValidationError, so if sample_weight is absent on the queried entity the chart request 500s instead of falling back to count(). The new stats test expects each 0.1-sampled event to contribute 10, which this code cannot produce. Once the allowlist is non-empty, error count charts for those projects will be zeroed, truncated, or failed.

findings.title: Error detection is a substring match and treats negations as errors
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query treats a discover query as error-only if the raw query string contains the substring event.type:error after lowercasing. That is true for negations and mixed filters: !event.type:error contains event.type:error, and so does event.type:error OR event.type:transaction. The helper says sample_weight must not be applied to transactions and that the check should err on the side of caution, but this match does the opposite of a parsed filter. For allowlisted projects, count() is then rewritten to sum(sample_weight) on a query that still includes transactions. That either fails in Snuba because the column is not on the transactions entity, or returns a meaningless sum. The stats endpoint does not catch SnubaError, so the chart 500s. The unit test only covers the exact strings event.type:error, event.type:transaction, and an empty query, so the false positive is untested.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the dataset and query actually executed
findings.body: _get_event_stats decides whether to upsample by passing the closed-over request dataset and request.GET query into is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, not scoped_dataset and the query argument this call actually runs. The dashboard widget split path in the same method invokes _get_event_stats with the discover dataset and a rewritten query such as (query) AND !event.type:transaction or AND event.type:transaction, while the closed-over dataset is metrics_performance or metrics_enhanced_performance (that branch only runs when metrics_enhanced is true). _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns false for metrics datasets, so those error-event widget queries never upsample even when every project is allowlisted. The request query is also not the executed query: a request containing event.type:error would mark the transaction-only probe eligible, and a request without that substring would skip an errors-only split. Dashboard error charts for allowlisted projects keep showing sampled counts, and the eligibility bit can disagree with the query sent to Snuba.

findings.title: Only an exact y-axis count() is rewritten; sort, equations, and filters stay raw
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling replaces a column only when its text is exactly count() (case-insensitive, stripped). In the top-events branch that rewritten list is passed as timeseries_columns / y_axes, but orderby=self.get_orderby(request) is left unchanged, so a normal sort=-count() still ranks groups by the raw count() aggregate while the plotted series is upsampled_count() as count. Top-N groups are chosen by sampled volume, so a low sample rate and high true volume group can be omitted; if the builder treats ORDER BY count() as a different aggregate from the alias, the top-events query errors instead. Equations (equation|count() * 2 and get_equation_list) and aggregate conditions in the query string (count():>N) are not rewritten either, so filters and equation series do not match the upsampled count series. Other count-derived y-axes such as epm() and eps() stay sampled, so one response can show an upsampled count beside a sampled rate. Columns that are already aliased, such as count() as errors, also fail the exact match and silently skip upsampling.

findings.title: Shared cache around an in-memory option read slows and can fail stats
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects calls cache.get and cache.set on Sentry's shared cache (Redis in production) on every events-stats query, including each dashboard split subquery, to avoid options.get of issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist. That option read is already a process-local dict lookup, so the cache adds a network round trip on a hot endpoint instead of removing work. Cache errors are not caught here, and OrganizationEventsStatsEndpoint does not catch them either, so a Redis timeout fails the chart. Keys are one per organization plus hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))), which is high-cardinality, and Python hash() is not a collision-resistant digest, so a collision would reuse another project set's allowlist boolean and could enable sum(sample_weight) for a set that is not fully allowlisted. invalidate_upsampling_cache is never called and can delete only one exact key, so it does not flush eligibility after an allowlist change. The docstring on _are_all_projects_error_upsampled, which says each call reads the latest configuration, is false once this 60-second cache is in front of it.

findings.title: upsampled_count is a public discover aggregate and bypasses the allowlist
findings.body: upsampled_count is registered on Discover's function converter without private=True, unlike the neighboring function in the same list (private defaults to false). It therefore becomes a user-facing function on every discover endpoint that shares this converter, not only the allowlisted stats path. Clients can request yAxis=upsampled_count(), or use it in other discover and alert queries, for projects that are not allowlisted and for queries that include transactions. The aggregate itself has no allowlist or dataset guard and always emits sum(sample_weight), so a missing column becomes a Snuba error and the gate in organization_events_stats is bypassable. It also sets default_result_type to number while count() is an integer, so series metadata changes type. If private functions are rejected by the same column parser the stats rewrite uses, marking it private will 400 the rewrite; the weight sum should be applied inside the query builder under the allowlist check rather than exposed as a public function.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink committed without .gitmodules
findings.body: This pull request adds a gitlink at sentry-repo pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a, which is the PR base, and does not add a .gitmodules entry or URL. A submodule pointer without a URL cannot be checked out. git submodule update, CI jobs that clone recursively, and tools that reject unexpected gitlinks will fail, and the link is unrelated to error upsampling. Remove the gitlink before merge.

findings.title: Upsampling tests assert a 10x count the fixtures never produce
findings.body: test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects stores events with client_sample_rate 0.1 and asserts each bucket count is 10. The factory only sets sample_rate to 0.1 and never sets sample_weight to 10, and no test inspects the SnQL or the stored column, so the assertion does not prove upsampling and fails unless an out-of-diff processor inverts the rate. The unit tests never call is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, never seed or clear the new cache, and never cover !event.type:error, mixed event.type:error OR event.type:transaction, dataset=errors (which the helper always rewrites), events missing sample_weight, or topEvents sorted by count(). Those are the paths that currently mis-apply or skip the rewrite.
